0.content:
General of the Tenryou Commission and Heizou's direct superior. She has "few positive words" for him: he chases his own schemes, keeps vanishing and once had to be found through a private detective agency. The only reason she has not reined him in is that he delivers results. He finds her the most serious person in the Commission and wishes she would give everyone breathing room. He also defends her fiercely: when rumours said she signed Ryuuji's conviction to please the Kujou Clan, he showed that she had in fact commuted Ryuuji's death sentence to temporary detention, the most a principled officer could do under pressure. When the Traveler vouched for him, she made the Traveler his temporary supervisor and handed him Sango's complaint letter.

Their famous bout at the station tournament: after Heizou won the bracket barehanded, Sara challenged him at fifty paces, bow against fists, with no Visions allowed. He caught her arrow just short of his heart, which by the rules meant she won. She said few could catch her arrows and that he would do great things "should you be more disciplined." She now assigns him the cases the Doushin cannot crack, asks how certain he is, and expects a clean debrief.

1.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: Sango and the Bantan Sango Detective Agency
1.content:
Heizou and Sango "struck an instant chord" and founded the "Bantan Sango & Heizou Detective Agency" in Hanamizaka, Inazuma City. They split because Sango believes a detective's whole mission is the truth, while Heizou believes something can matter more than the truth: stopping harm before it happens. His name was taken off the sign. Today Sango says she would be happiest if he went missing for a hundred years, calls him a yappy dog in her path to the "Temple of Truth", and writes complaint letters about him. Her assistant Ryuuji, an orphan and former Doushin, is fond of Heizou but keeps his distance in public at Sango's request.

The rivalry hides respect. Heizou quietly sends minor cases her way to support the business, and in 5.7 he relied on Sango's covert investigation for evidence. He is said to be the only person who can follow her train of thought. When he left, he told her "Some things will always be more important than the truth"; after the Ryuuji Case was reopened, she admitted she finally understood.

2.content: A shrine maiden at the Grand Narukami Shrine and Heizou's older, distant cousin (their surnames share the characters for "wild deer"). She also chases the runaway ninja Sayu, and says Sayu can be an even bigger headache than Heizou. She remembers him as a rule-breaker who was always in trouble, never expected him to become a detective, and complains she can never find him. He calls her "cuz" and explains himself to her patiently, a rare thing for him, to keep her out of trouble. When she was ready to march on the Commission over his lack of promotion, he talked her down with a joke about the hairs on the back of his hand: inmates who know his name outnumber those who know any Yoriki. She is his link to his father: he sent his tournament medal through her.

3.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: The Vision and the Green Pebble
3.content:
Heizou rarely talks about his unhappy childhood. At a festival he befriended a bright boy who claimed to be a rich merchant's son and brought him books from Sumeru and toys from Fontaine. As they grew up, Heizou noticed the boy's filthy clothes, asked him outright, and learned everything was stolen, and that they had first met because the boy meant to rob him. Heizou ended the friendship and threw out every gift except one of a pair of green pebbles the two had fished from a stream. A year later, at the same festival, he found his friend collapsed in his own blood, stabbed by a ruffian who tried to steal his purse. The purse held no Mora, only the other green pebble. Dying, the friend said he had come to see Heizou too.

In his rage Heizou named the true enemy: not his friend's theft or the killer's crime, but "sin" itself, the shadow over the world that mixes deceit into friendship and cuts lives short. A month later he left home before dawn with a farewell note. He carried a green stone again, this time a Vision standing for his resolve.

4.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: "Cyclone" and the Police Station Jail
4.content:
At the Police Station Jail the best-known name is not any Yoriki's or the General's, or even, in there, the Raiden Shogun's, but Doushin Shikanoin Heizou's. Crooks blamed "that detective" for their capture until they learned he was one man who had caught countless skilled criminals. They decided he must be something more than human, and stopped speaking ill of him. Even crime lords now use a pseudonym for him, "Cyclone", which petty criminals explain as "a calamity, a plague upon all us crooks." He has refused promotion so that his name keeps spreading. When he joined, he levelled the backlog of cold cases, "Mt. Coldcase", for practice.

The reputation works as a tool. The old trader Iba confessed the moment he heard Heizou was on his case: "what else can you do when a 'Cyclone' is heading your way?" Heizou jokes that at this rate the name "Cyclone" is really going to stick.

5.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: Watatsumi Island and the Missing Thing
5.content:
Hangout Event (2.8). Heizou disappeared, and the Tenryou Commission discreetly commissioned the Bantan Sango Detective Agency to find him; Ryuuji passed the job to the Traveler. They found him on Watatsumi, having let Nobushi "capture" him to study them. He was chasing a dream he had had on his first night there during the war: "Something vital is missing on this island." Nobushi loot pointed to raided caravans. Gorou blamed a Ritou merchant, but Heizou sensed a lie. Tailing caravan chief Todoroki by night, they found smuggled medicinal herbs (Qingxin, Glaze Lilies) that Watatsumi's soldiers had "seized", and heard from captured Nobushi that 'pirates' on a massive ship, captained by an eye-patched woman, had taken a load of Sango Pearls and Crystal Marrow off them.

Confronted, Todoroki explained that his elder son died in the war and his younger son died for lack of medicine, because barren Watatsumi pays crushing tariffs on herbs from Ritou. A Kanjou Commission bill exempting such goods was months away. Gorou said he would never let them take Todoroki. Heizou announced he would just enjoy a longer holiday there until the bill passed, kept the secret, and made Gorou promise not to restrict the Traveler's freedom either. His final answer to the dream: the island's missing vitality had not vanished but "evaporated" into its brave, stubborn people.

6.content: Hangout Event (2.8). Years ago Takatsukasa Isamu, head of the Police Station and rising star of the Takatsukasa Clan, died of a novel poison. His devoted aide Ryuuji was convicted within a week; Kujou Sara signed the conviction but commuted the death sentence. Sango then caught the forensic doctor Shiroyama, who left a confession saying Isamu had blackmailed him through his pregnant wife into developing a poison, and then hanged himself. Unconvinced, Sango spent years demanding the files and finally filed a complaint against Heizou. Heizou let the Traveler, as his supervisor, re-examine everything, and kept stressing "everything the Police Station has". The Traveler caught the hint: Heizou held evidence of his own.

7.content: Hangout Event (2.8). An anti-fraud public-awareness play Heizou got approved by Commission headquarters, on the grounds that preventing even one person from being scammed is worth it. He recruited two convicted fraudsters as the "scammers": Etsu, a flirtatious con artist doing community service at the Grand Narukami Shrine, whom he bargained down from five days of credit to three; and the elderly former guild master Iba, whom Heizou had helped get probation, cornered by a promise to his granddaughter Kazumi. Iba grumbled that Heizou is crafty "just like your father". As the "victim", Paimon suggested Arataki Itto, who ignored the script. Heizou narrated live as "Doushin Arataki" nearly handed over a fake 500,000 Mora check for ten thousand Onikabuto.

8.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu
8.content: Heizou has smuggled roasted Lavender Melons to Itto in his cell more than once, at Shinobu's request; Itto mistook him for a fellow inmate and for a Lavender Melon seller at the station. Heizou once heard Itto singing in prison: terrible lyrics, a good voice. He admires the Arataki Gang for taking in anyone, and buys intelligence from Shinobu, who in turn asks him to speak up for her when she bails the boys out. Shinobu notes she has never seen him patrol or arrest anyone. In the 4.6 limited event he brought two baskets of Lavender Melons to Itto's music festival: one from Kujou Sara, one chipped in by Doushin who had arrested Itto and by his former cellmates.

9.content: The former head of the Tenryou Commission. During the war he secretly sent Heizou to assess Sangonomiya's military strength; Heizou, already tired of him, treated it as a paid holiday and planned to invent a report. After the Vision Hunt Decree ended and Takayuki lost power, Sara put Heizou in charge of building the case against him so she would not be accused of bias. In Takayuki's secret warehouse Heizou found the Ryuuji Case evidence. He believes Takayuki kept the poison formula in case he needed to make someone else disappear, but says one hidden log proves nothing in court.

10.content: Heizou calls Kazuha "a solid guy": with his help, a locked chest of clues burst open. He concludes the wind is to Kazuha what intuition is to him. Under the Vision Hunt Decree he could have arrested the wanted ronin; now that it is repealed he can only invite Kazuha to the Commission to talk over cases. Kazuha warns people not to be fooled by Heizou's happy-go-lucky air, because on a case his restless energy becomes razor-sharp focus.

11.comment: Shikanoin Heizou: Watatsumi's Watchers: Gorou and Kokomi
11.content: Kokomi was astonished to see a man in Tenryou Commission uniform touring Watatsumi: too brazen for a samurai, too conspicuous for a spy. She had him watched, judged him a self-styled detective with no interest in military, government or trade, and let him stay. Gorou kept soldiers on him everywhere, calls him a sneaky detective who never seems to work, and wonders if his talent hides a scheme. Heizou jokes that he was just a boring tourist. After the herb-smuggling affair, Gorou admitted it was impossible to hide anything from him.
